chapter: Settle the Terms, Not the Family Drama
subtitle: 先谈价，别谈表哥
sentences: Xie Linzhou's invitation lay on the table all night.
Mother had someone weigh it down with her abacus. That way, she said, the bad luck couldn't rise to the surface.
By the next morning, she was clicking the beads back and forth at a furious pace while I sat opposite her and listened to her reject my plan for the third time.
"I'm not taking the account books," I said. "I'll only go and hear what he has to say."
"And you think you'll understand what he's really saying?"
"Mother, I helped Wen Li escape her wedding yesterday."
"That's exactly why I'm worried."
She swept the beads aside and turned to Chuntao. "Find the young miss something sturdy to wear. Nothing red."
"Mother!"
"If someone puts you in another bridal sedan, I'd at least like to know which one is my daughter."
A laugh escaped Chuntao before she hurriedly ducked her head.

Mother pushed a sheet covered in boat numbers across the table. It wasn't an original. Uncle Qin had copied the details from an old hauling agency register: three boats that left Dongping Wharf on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month, complete with the boat owners, cargo volumes, and the people who handled the shipments.
"You can ask him about this," Mother said. "But don't let the Xie family get their hands on the original tickets. And don't so much as mention Accountant Song's letter."
"Why not?"
"He asked you to bring old accounts. He didn't say which ones. The Jiang family runs a business. We have plenty of books."
Then she pulled the sheet back and wrote two characters on the reverse: FOR QUESTIONS.
"What's that supposed to mean?" I asked.
"In case you lose your head again. One look at those words should remind you that you're there to ask questions, not confess to a crime."
I had no comeback for that.

To keep me from losing my head on my own, Mother enlisted my second and third aunts. Second Aunt was the one who'd marched me out of the marquis's residence yesterday. Third Aunt was an even more formidable force. The moment she arrived, she asked whether the Xie family planned to serve lunch.
"Bring food either way," she declared. "Never argue with someone on an empty stomach. You'll be at a disadvantage."
And so, before noon, the marquis's reception hall received me, two aunts, Chuntao, and a box of mung bean cakes.
Xie Linzhou sat in the seat of honor, dressed in ordinary dark teal robes. His wedding finery had disappeared somewhere. I imagined it would be rather embarrassing to hang it back up.
His eyebrows twitched when he saw my aunts.
"Mingyue, I invited you."
"I know." I sat down. "My aunts were passing by and thought they'd see how our dear cousin was doing after getting married."
Third Aunt was already opening the cake box. "Linzhou, have a cake. You can't have slept well last night."
"Thank you, Aunt. I'm not hungry."
"Looking that pale, and you're still not hungry?"
Xie Linzhou was silent for a moment before signaling a steward to bring tea.
Neither aunt showed any intention of leaving. And he could hardly detain me again in front of them. We stared at one another, neither willing to mention yesterday's bridal sedan first.
In the end, Xie Linzhou broke the silence. "Did you bring the Jiang family's old accounts?"
I laid the copied list of boat numbers on the table.
"I brought this for now."
He gave it a glance. "This isn't what I asked for."

"Which book do you want, Cousin?" I asked. "We have accounts for the grain shipments three years ago, and accounts for the New Year gifts the Jiang family bought your household. Why don't you make a list? I'll go home and look through them."
Third Aunt nodded. "Exactly. Be specific."
Ignoring her, Xie Linzhou fixed his eyes on me. "Your mother has the original vouchers Accountant Song left behind."
My heart gave a jump.
So he did know.
Mother had wondered how he knew about the old tickets she'd never shown an outsider. Now he knew not only that they existed but also who had left them behind.
"Accountant Song died last year," I said. "Surely you don't get to decide what he left behind."

"Mingyue." Xie Linzhou softened his voice. "Your mother doesn't understand affairs of the court. Now that the old case has been reopened, the Ministry of Punishments has the private ledger, and the Jiang family appears in it. If you produce documents that contradict the official records, you'll only make things harder for your family."
He spoke calmly, almost kindly. If I hadn't remembered the sword that had nearly been drawn yesterday, I might actually have mistaken his words for concern.
"Then why are you so eager to get the originals?" I asked.
"I'm afraid your mother is being misled."
"By whom?"
"Wen Li."
There it was.
"Yesterday, she used you as a stand-in bride and took that ledger to accuse me," Xie Linzhou said. "The Jiang Trading House is named in that ledger. Did she not know, or did she simply not care?"
That struck a nerve.
I could still hear Wen Li saying, "I was afraid you'd refuse." It made me angry even now. She had used me. But that didn't automatically make Xie Linzhou the trustworthy one.
I lifted my teacup but didn't drink.
"I know she manipulated me. We already had that argument yesterday."
"And you're still helping her?"

"I didn't come to help her accuse you. I'm here about the Jiang family." I pushed the sheet forward. "These three boats left Dongping Wharf on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. Yet your old ledger says the Jiang Trading House delivered grain to the granary on the ninth day of the twelfth month. Have you seen the government granary's delivery receipt?"
Xie Linzhou made no move to touch the list.
"The two records may not refer to the same shipment."
"Exactly." I nodded. "That's why we need to check with the boat owners and granary clerks from back then. You can't see 'Jiang Trading House' in a ledger and decide my mother must be guilty."
At last, he raised his eyes.
"You've learned how to keep accounts lately, I see."
"Business is slow at home. I have time on my hands."
"The Jiang family is still able to do business only because I chose not to pursue the matter."
The moment those words left his mouth, Second Aunt set down her teacup.
"Linzhou, that's no way to speak. If Jiang Trading House broke the law, the authorities can investigate. If it didn't, since when is its innocence a favor granted by you?"
He had to backtrack. "You've misunderstood me, Aunt. I only meant to warn Mingyue not to drag her family into this."

He gestured for a steward to fetch a document. It was a prepared written statement saying that Jiang Trading House had been commissioned to transport eight thousand shi of grain and had checked every shipping document for accuracy.
The final line had been left blank for the signature and seal of the proprietor of Jiang Trading House.
I read it twice.
"So you want my mother to vouch for that official register from the twelfth month?"
"It merely confirms the portion handled by your trading house."
"But it doesn't mention the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. It just says eight thousand shi. How do we know which day's accounts someone might attach it to later?"
Xie Linzhou's outstretched hand froze in midair.
I put the document back down.

"Cousin, if you truly want to help, bring in whoever received the grain. Who shipped it, who accepted it, and when it entered the granary—we can compare the records. How does getting my mother to sign this help anyone?"
Third Aunt finally found her opening. "Quite right. If you're asking a woman to sign something this important, the least you can do is serve lunch first."
I nearly spat out my tea.

Xie Linzhou probably wanted the meeting over as badly as I did. He put away the statement and stopped asking about Accountant Song's tickets. Instead, he asked, "What has Wen Li offered you, to make you defend her like this?"
"Nothing."
"Then you're still trying to spite me."
I looked at him and suddenly decided he was even harder to reason with than the man in the original novel.

In his version of the world, Wen Li had run away from her wedding to get his attention, and I was helping her to make him jealous. It must be exhausting being a man who thought everything was about him.

"Cousin," I said, "I bullied Wen Li because of you before. That was wrong. If she does something wrong now, I'll take it up with her too. But the dates on the Jiang family's boat tickets won't change depending on whom I like."
The smile faded from his face.
"Mingyue, do you really think the person you've befriended is good?"
"I never said she was."
I rose and bowed slightly to my aunts. "I only said we need to find out what the accounts actually show."
Only after we left the reception hall did my legs begin to feel weak. Chuntao steadied me and whispered, "Miss, weren't you scared in there?"
"Terrified."
"Then why did you say so much?"
"If I kept quiet, he might pin all eight thousand shi on me. I couldn't pay that back even if I sold you."
"Miss!"
"I'm joking. If anyone gets sold, it'll be me first. I eat more, so I probably weigh more."
Chuntao looked torn between laughing and crying. Up ahead, Second Aunt called, "Stop dawdling! We didn't even get any cake at the Xie house, and we still have to cook when we get home."
We had barely reached the mouth of the lane when Third Aunt stopped and produced a scrap of paper folded into a triangle from her sleeve.
"An old maid serving tea slipped this under my saucer. I thought it was the kitchen menu."
I unfolded it. There was only one sentence: Don't let Accountant Song's tickets enter the Xie residence.
It was signed with a tiny character: Zhou.
My fingers tightened around the corner of the note.
Could the unnamed helper Wen Li had mentioned yesterday still be inside the marquis's residence?
At dusk, I met Wen Li at a small teahouse in the west of the city.
She sat at a table overlooking the street, with two cups of tea before her. When I came in, she looked past me first, then down at my hands.
"Did you take the accounts?"
"Not the originals. And could you stop checking my family's finances every time you see me?"
I placed the triangular note in front of her. Wen Li's smile vanished at once.
"You recognize the writing?" I asked.
She folded the note back along its creases and slowly nodded.
"I do."
"Then you owe me an explanation."
Wen Li slipped the note into her sleeve. "I owe you a great many explanations. But right now, what's most important is that no third person sees this note."
"Why?"
"Because the person who wrote it is still inside the residence."
She raised her head toward the other side of the street, then suddenly went still.
I followed her gaze. Two men in plain clothes stood beside a stall selling sugar figures. One of them reached down to adjust the sash at his waist.
I'd seen that same gesture at the marquis's gate that morning.
"Were you followed?" Wen Li asked.
"I thought you were the one being followed."
After a moment's silence, she drained her tea in one gulp.
"Then we won't leave by the back door today."
"Why not?"
"The back alley's too quiet. We'll go out onto the main street."
"And you think nothing can happen where there are people?"
"Not necessarily." Wen Li stood. "But if something does happen, at least there'll be witnesses."
Somehow, that didn't make me feel any safer.
translations: 谢临舟那张帖子在桌上放了一夜。
我娘让人把它压在算盘底下，说这样晦气就翻不上来了。
第二天一早，算盘珠子被她拨得噼啪响，我坐在对面，听她把我的主意否决了第三遍。
“我不带账本去。”我说，“只去听听他究竟想干什么。”
“你听得明白？”
“娘，我昨天还帮温梨逃了婚。”
“所以我才不放心。”
她把算盘一合，望向春桃：“给小姐换身结实点的衣裳。不要红的。”
“你若再被抬进花轿里，我好歹能认出哪个是你。”
春桃没憋住，笑出声，又赶紧低头。
母亲把一张写满船号的纸推给我。不是原件，只是秦叔从脚行旧簿中誊出的名单：十一月十八日从东平码头起航的三条船，船主、货量、经手人都列得清清楚楚。
“你可以拿这个问他。”母亲说，“但别让谢家拿到原票。宋账房那封信，你连提都不要提。”
“为什么？”
“他请你带旧账，没说哪一本。姜家做生意，账多着呢。”
她说完又把纸收回去，在背面写下两个字：备询。
“什么意思？”我问。
“万一你又犯糊涂，看到这两个字，好记得你是去问话，不是去认罪。”
我服了。
为了防止我独自犯糊涂，母亲请来了二姑母和三姑母。二姑母是昨日把我从侯府领出来的那位；三姑母更厉害，进门先问谢家今日管不管饭。
“管不管都带点吃的，”她说，“别空着肚子跟人吵，容易吃亏。”
于是午时未到，侯府花厅迎来我、两位姑母、春桃，以及一盒绿豆糕。
谢临舟坐在主位，换了件墨青色常服。那身新郎喜服不知收去了哪里，想来再挂出来也挺丢人。
他看见两位姑母，眉头微微一动。
“明月，我请的是你。”
“我知道。”我坐下，“姑母们路过，顺便看看表哥成亲之后过得好不好。”
三姑母已经打开食盒：“临舟，吃糕。你昨夜肯定没睡好。”
“多谢姑母，我不饿。”
“脸色都青了，还不饿？”
谢临舟沉默了一息，向旁边的管事示意上茶。
两位姑母不走。他也不能当着她们的面把我再扣一次。我们互相看着，谁都不肯先提昨日那顶花轿。
最后还是谢临舟先开口：“姜家的旧账带来了吗？”
我将那张誊写的船号清单放到桌上。
“先带了这个。”
他看了一眼：“我要的不是这个。”
“表哥到底要哪本？”我问，“三年前的粮运有账，姜府给侯府买年礼也有账。要不您写个单子，我回家慢慢找。”
三姑母点头：“对。话要说清楚。”
谢临舟不看她，只盯着我：“你娘有宋账房留下的底票。”
我心里一跳。
果然。
昨夜我娘问他怎么知道，她怀里有的是一份没有给过外人的旧票。如今谢临舟不仅知道有票，连宋账房的名字都说了出来。
“宋账房去年就死了。”我说，“他留下什么，不该由你先说了算吧？”
“明月。”谢临舟放缓声音，“你娘不懂朝堂的事。旧案如今重翻，刑部拿着那本私账，你们姜家也在上面。再拿出一份与官册抵触的票据，只会让姜家更难脱身。”
他说得不急不慢。要不是我记得昨天那把剑差点出鞘，兴许真会以为表哥在替我操心。
“既然这样，表哥为何急着要原件？”我问。
“怕你娘被人误导。”
“谁误导？”
“温梨。”
来了。
“她昨日拿你当新娘，又带着账去告我。”谢临舟说，“账上有姜记，是她不知道，还是她根本不在乎？”
这话说中了。
温梨在我耳边说过的那句“怕你不同意”，到现在想起来还气人。她的确利用了我。但这不代表谢临舟就是可信的那个。
我端起茶，没喝。
“我知道她算计我。昨天已经吵过了。”
“那你还帮她？”
“我没帮她告你。我今天来，是问姜家的事。”我把纸往前推了推，“这三条船，十一月十八日从东平码头启运。你那本旧账却写腊月初九由姜记运粮入仓。表哥见过官仓的收条吗？”
谢临舟没有伸手碰清单。
“两本账并不一定记的是同一批粮。”
“是。”我点头，“所以才要找当年的船主、仓吏核对。您总不能因为账上有‘姜记’两个字，就替我娘把错认了。”
他终于抬起眼。
“你最近倒是学会算账了。”
“家里没生意，闲着也是闲着。”
“姜家现在还能做生意，是因为我没有追究。”
这句话刚落地，二姑母就搁下了茶碗。
“临舟，话不能这么讲。姜记若真犯了事，自有官府查。若没犯，怎么成了你给的恩典？”
谢临舟只得改口：“姑母误会。我是在提醒明月别把家里也搭进去。”
他招手让管事取来一张纸。那是一份拟好的书面陈述，写着姜记当年受托运粮八千石，所有转运单据均由姜家核验无误。
最后一行留着空白，要姜记东家的签押。
我看了两遍。
“这不就是让我娘替那份腊月官册作保？”
“只是说明商号经手的部分。”
“可上面没写十一月十八，只写八千石。谁知道以后会被拿去配哪一天的账？”
谢临舟伸来的手停在半空。
我把纸放回去。
“表哥，真想帮忙，就让收粮的那个人出来说话。谁运的、谁接的、哪天入仓，一对便知道。叫我娘在这里签字，算什么帮忙？”
三姑母终于得着机会：“就是。你让一个妇道人家签这么大的事，起码先把饭端上来吧。”
我差点把茶喷出去。
谢临舟大概也想让这场见面赶紧结束。他收起陈述书，不再提宋账房的票，反倒问：“你今日这么替温梨说话，她给了你什么好处？”
“没有。”
“那就是你还想和我赌气。”
我望着他，突然觉得这人比书里还难讲道理。
在他的世界里，温梨逃婚是为了引他注意，我帮温梨是为了让他吃醋。一个男人把什么事都往自己身上想，也挺辛苦的。
“表哥，”我说，“我以前为了你欺负过温梨，那是我的错。她现在做错事，我也会同她算。可姜家的船票，不会因为我喜欢谁就换个日期。”
他脸上的笑意淡了。
“明月，你以为你如今结交的是个好人？”
“我没说她是好人。”
我站起来，向两位姑母欠身，“我只说，账得查清。”
出了花厅，我才觉得腿有些软。春桃扶了我一把，小声问：“小姐刚才不怕吗？”
“怕啊。”
“那您还说那么多？”
“少说两句，回头他把八千石都算我头上怎么办？我卖了你也赔不起。”
“小姐！”
“开玩笑的。真要卖先卖我自己，起码吃得多，分量重。”
春桃哭笑不得，二姑母在前面喊：“别磨蹭，谢府糕没吃上，回家还要做饭呢。”
我们刚走到巷口，三姑母忽然停住，从袖子里抽出一张折成三角的纸。
“方才有个端茶的老嬷嬷把这个压在我碗托底下，我还当是厨房的菜单。”
我打开一看，上面只有一句话：别让宋账房的票进谢府。
落款是个极小的“周”字。
我抓紧纸角。
昨日温梨没有说出名字的那个帮手，难道还留在侯府里？
傍晚，我在城西一间小茶肆见到温梨。
她坐在临街的位置，面前摆着两盏茶。见我进来，先看我身后，再看我的手。
“账带去了？”
“没带原件。你别一见面就查我家底。”
我把那张三角纸放到她面前。温梨的笑容一下收住了。
“你认得这字？”我问。
她将纸叠回原样，缓缓点头。
“认得。”
“那你欠我一个解释。”
温梨把纸收进袖口：“我欠你很多解释。但现在最要紧的，是让这张纸别再被第三个人看见。”
“为什么？”
“因为写字的人还没出府。”
她抬头望向街对面，目光忽然停了。
我顺着看过去，两个便衣男子站在卖糖人的摊子旁。其中一个抬手整了整腰间衣带。
那动作，我早上在侯府门口见过。
“你被人跟了？”温梨问。
“我以为是你被跟了。”
她沉默一瞬，端起自己的茶一饮而尽。
“那今天别从后门走。”
“为什么？”
“后门太安静。我们从正街出去。”
“正街人多，就不会出事？”
“不一定。”温梨起身，“但出了事，至少有人看见。”
这话一点都不让人安心。

annotations.explain: lay 是 lie（躺、处于某处）的过去式，不是 lay（放置）的现在式；描述物品静置时常用 lay。
annotations.example: The letter lay unopened on her desk.

annotations.explain: have + 人 + 动词原形表示安排别人做事；weigh something down with something 表示用重物压住物品。with her abacus 中的 with 引出所用工具，不能把 weigh down 理解成“称重量”。
annotations.example: She had a servant weigh the papers down with a book.

annotations.explain: That way 用来解释做某事的方法及其效果，是口语叙述中很常见的衔接表达。
annotations.example: Keep a copy. That way, you won't lose the evidence.

annotations.explain: 可指东西浮上来，也可比喻问题或情绪浮现；此处与“晦气”构成幽默说法。
annotations.example: Old doubts began to rise to the surface.

annotations.explain: by + 时间点表示不迟于该时或截至那时；此处交代时间推进。
annotations.example: By dawn, everyone had heard the news.

annotations.explain: 常见固定副词短语，可描述往返运动、反复讨论或争执。
annotations.example: They argued back and forth for an hour.

annotations.explain: at a ... pace 表示进行速度；furious 在这里强调猛烈、急促，不一定是“愤怒的”。
annotations.example: The clerks worked at a frantic pace.

annotations.explain: for the + 序数词 + time 表示某事发生到第几次；常表达叙述者的无奈。
annotations.example: He asked the same question for the third time.

annotations.explain: what someone has to say 在 hear / listen to 后构成常见搭配，强调听取对方意见或解释。
annotations.example: Let's hear what she has to say first.

annotations.explain: 进行时可强调此刻言语所传达的意图；really 暗示字面意思之外的潜台词。
annotations.example: Pay attention to what he's really saying.

annotations.explain: That's exactly why ... 用来指出前述理由恰好支持自己的相反立场。
annotations.example: You trust him too much. That's exactly why I'm worried.

annotations.explain: sweep something aside 表示快速将物体拨到一旁，画面中表现母亲迅速结束算账并转向春桃。
annotations.example: She swept the papers aside.

annotations.explain: something + 形容词 + to do 是不定代词后置修饰；sturdy 在衣物语境指耐穿结实。
annotations.example: Bring something warm to wear.

annotations.phrase: I'd at least like to know
annotations.explain: I'd = I would；would like to 比 want 更委婉，在母亲的玩笑中形成反讽。
annotations.example: I'd at least like to hear your side of it.

annotations.explain: a laugh escaped someone 表示笑声不自觉地冒出来，比 laughed 更有画面感。
annotations.example: A nervous laugh escaped him.

annotations.explain: duck one's head 指快速低头，常表现躲避视线、害羞或回避。
annotations.example: She ducked her head to hide a smile.

annotations.explain: push/slide something across the table 是自然的动作描写搭配，across 强调横穿表面。
annotations.example: He slid the contract across the desk.

annotations.explain: original 用作名词表示原件；与 copy（副本、誊本）形成法律和证据语境的重要区分。
annotations.example: We only have a copy, not the original.

annotations.explain: complete with + 名词表示附带、配有某些细节，适合描述清单或文件的完整信息。
annotations.example: The package arrived complete with instructions.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时 had copied 用于回顾当前叙述之前已完成的动作。
annotations.example: He had checked the list before the meeting.

annotations.explain: 固定表达 get one's hands on，强调设法获得某物，常带争夺或急切意味。
annotations.example: Don't let them get their hands on the letter.

annotations.explain: not so much as + 动词原形表示连最轻微的动作都不允许或不发生，强调程度。
annotations.example: Don't so much as open that box.

annotations.explain: run a business 是固定动宾搭配，run 此处不是“跑”。
annotations.example: Her family has run a business for generations.

annotations.explain: plenty of + 可数复数或不可数名词，语气比 many/much 更轻松。
annotations.example: We have plenty of time to check.

annotations.explain: the reverse 指纸张、硬币等物体的背面；也可用于 on the reverse side。
annotations.example: The date was written on the reverse.

annotations.explain: What's that supposed to mean? 常不只是求解释，也可表示质疑、困惑或不满。
annotations.example: What's that supposed to mean, exactly?

annotations.explain: in case + 从句说明采取预防措施的理由，不等于 if（条件触发）。
annotations.example: Keep the receipt in case they ask for it.

annotations.explain: 惯用语 lose one's head 指紧张时失去冷静，不是字面掉头；本章反复出现形成角色笑点。
annotations.example: Don't lose your head when they question you.

annotations.explain: one look at ... 强调短暂注视即可引发想法；可写 One look at his face told me ...。
annotations.example: One look at the seal told her something was wrong.

annotations.explain: confess to + 名词或动名词，固定介词 to 不应省略。
annotations.example: He refused to confess to a crime he hadn't committed.

annotations.explain: comeback 可指机智回应、回嘴；have no comeback 表示一时找不到话反驳。
annotations.example: For once, I had no comeback.

annotations.explain: on one's own 表示独自或独立完成；此处和 lose your head 组合制造幽默。
annotations.example: She went to the office on her own.

annotations.explain: enlist someone 表示争取某人协助，不一定与从军有关；常见搭配 enlist help / support。
annotations.example: She enlisted her cousins to help.

annotations.explain: march someone out of ... 带有命令式、毫不拖泥带水的意味。
annotations.example: The guard marched him out of the room.

annotations.explain: formidable 指令人敬畏、难以应对，不只是“强大”；把姑母形容成 force 是轻喜剧夸张。
annotations.example: My grandmother was an even more formidable opponent.

annotations.explain: the moment + 完整句子表示“一……就……”，相当于 as soon as。
annotations.example: The moment I saw him, I knew something was wrong.

annotations.explain: either way 表示两种情况结果都一样，是高频口语表达。
annotations.example: We'll go either way.

annotations.explain: on an empty stomach 是固定说法，常指没吃东西时做事或服药。
annotations.example: Don't drink that tea on an empty stomach.

annotations.explain: be at a disadvantage 是固定搭配；相对的表达是 have an advantage。
annotations.example: Without the documents, we'd be at a disadvantage.

annotations.explain: And so 在叙事里表示前面一系列安排带来的结果，语气较自然。
annotations.example: And so we arrived with two witnesses.

annotations.explain: seat of honor 指宴席或正式会面中最尊贵的位置，体现身份和礼序。
annotations.example: The host sat in the seat of honor.

annotations.explain: finery 是华丽衣服或饰物的集合名词，通常不可数。
annotations.example: She had put away her wedding finery.

annotations.explain: hang something up 表示把衣物挂起，back 强调恢复原位；此处是叙述者的嘲讽想象。
annotations.example: He hung the cloak back up.

annotations.explain: twitch 描写短促、不自主的小动作，常用来暗示人物压抑情绪。
annotations.example: His eyelid twitched at the remark.

annotations.explain: pass by 表示经过某地；与 just passing by 连用常是委婉说辞。
annotations.example: We were just passing by.

annotations.explain: thought we'd ... 表示“我们想来……”，比 We decided to 更随意，常用于找理由。
annotations.example: I thought I'd stop in and say hello.

annotations.explain: can't have + 过去分词表示对过去情况有较强把握的否定推测，并非“没有能力睡”。
annotations.example: You can't have known about the letter.

annotations.explain: Looking that pale 是口语中的省略/分词式开头，结合后半句理解为“脸色这么苍白，竟然还不饿？”；不要孤立地将 looking 视为正在“看”。
annotations.example: Looking this tired, and you're still working?

annotations.phrase: signaling a steward to bring tea
annotations.explain: signal someone to do something 是常见结构，用动作代替口头命令。
annotations.example: She signaled the servant to close the door.

annotations.explain: show no/any intention of + doing，介词 of 后接动名词。
annotations.example: He showed no intention of apologizing.

annotations.explain: could hardly ... 表示在情境下难以这么做，不是“努力地”。
annotations.example: He could hardly refuse in front of everyone.

annotations.explain: neither + 形容词/分词作补充说明，描写双方共同状态。
annotations.example: They sat there, neither willing to speak first.

annotations.explain: break the silence 是非常常用的叙事搭配。
annotations.example: At last, she broke the silence.

annotations.explain: 此处 laid 是及物动词 lay（放置）的过去式：lay–laid–laid；第1句 lay on the table 则是不及物动词 lie（平放）的过去式：lie–lay–lain。两套动词形态非常容易混淆。
annotations.example: She laid the file on the desk, where it lay unopened all night.

annotations.explain: for now 表示眼下如此，未来可能改变。
annotations.example: This copy will do for now.

annotations.explain: give something a glance 是轻快的动作描写；同义有 glance at。
annotations.example: She gave the note a quick glance.

annotations.explain: look through + 文件/书本，表示逐页查看或寻找信息，不是字面“看穿”。
annotations.example: I'll look through the old records tonight.

annotations.explain: be specific 用于要求别人提供准确细节，是高频口语/职场表达。
annotations.example: Please be specific about which receipt you need.

annotations.explain: leave something behind 可指物理遗留，也可指某人去世后留下的物品。
annotations.example: The documents he left behind became crucial.

annotations.explain: heart gives a jump 描写突然紧张或惊讶的瞬间；不是身体真正跳动一次。
annotations.example: My heart gave a jump when I heard his name.

annotations.explain: 助动词 did 在肯定句中用于强调，与前面怀疑或猜测形成对照。
annotations.example: So you did see the letter.

annotations.phrase: not only that they existed but also
annotations.explain: not only ... but also ... 是并列强调结构；注意连接的成分需平行。
annotations.example: She knew not only the date but also the name.

annotations.explain: Surely ... 常用于说话者坚信对方不该这么做，带质疑或施压。
annotations.example: Surely you don't expect me to sign this.

annotations.explain: get to + 动词表示有机会或权利做某事，质疑句中强调权限。
annotations.example: Who gets to decide which document is valid?

annotations.explain: soften one's voice 描写语气转变，可能是真诚也可能是策略；需结合行为判断。
annotations.example: She softened her voice to calm the child.

annotations.explain: 现在完成时被动：has/have been + 过去分词，强调旧案目前处于重新启动后的状态。
annotations.example: The investigation has been reopened.

annotations.explain: contradict + 名词直接作宾语，不接 with；指内容不一致而非自动证明一方造假。
annotations.example: The two receipts contradict each other.

annotations.explain: make + 宾语 + 形容词 是使役结构；harder 是比较级。
annotations.example: That decision will make things harder for us.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时的虚拟条件句：If + had(n't) done，主句往往是 would/might have done。
annotations.example: If I hadn't checked, I might have signed it.

annotations.explain: might have + 过去分词表示对过去反事实情境的可能结果；mistake A for B 是固定搭配。
annotations.example: I might have mistaken silence for agreement.

annotations.explain: be eager to do something = 急于或渴望做某事；so 强调程度。
annotations.example: Why are they so eager to see the originals?

annotations.explain: be being + 过去分词是进行时被动；这里强调可能持续发生的误导。
annotations.example: She is being misled by incomplete data.

annotations.explain: 小说中常用的独立短句，表示预料中的话题或真相终于出现，不能机械翻为“它在那里”。
annotations.example: There it was—the accusation I'd expected.

annotations.explain: stand-in 作名词或定语指临时代替他人的人，常见 stand-in actor。
annotations.example: She was asked to be a stand-in for the ceremony.

annotations.phrase: Did she not know, or did she simply not care
annotations.meaning: 她是不知道，还是根本不在乎
annotations.explain: A or B 并列疑问制造“无论哪种都不利”的修辞压力；不代表只有两种可能。
annotations.example: Did he forget, or did he choose not to answer?

annotations.explain: strike a nerve 表示碰到敏感问题，让人产生强烈情绪。
annotations.example: Her question struck a nerve.

annotations.phrase: It made me angry even now
annotations.meaning: 现在想起来仍让我生气
annotations.explain: even now 强调隔了一段时间后情绪仍未消散。
annotations.example: Even now, I regret trusting him.

annotations.explain: not automatically 反驳从一个事实跳到另一个结论的逻辑；是人物独立判断的关键。
annotations.example: One mistake doesn't automatically make someone guilty.

annotations.phrase: lifted my teacup but didn't drink
annotations.explain: 并列动作中的反差暗示犹豫或防备，属于叙事潜台词，不只是动作记录。
annotations.example: He picked up the pen but didn't sign.

annotations.explain: have an argument 表示发生争论；that argument 指双方都知道的上一场争执。
annotations.example: We've already had that argument.

annotations.explain: yet 在句首或分句开头表示强烈转折，常用于对比证据。
annotations.example: The receipt is dated May. Yet the ledger says June.

annotations.explain: 现在完成时询问截至目前是否有过相关经历或接触；此处质询证据来源。
annotations.example: Have you seen the original receipt?

annotations.explain: make no move to + 动词原形，强调拒绝或刻意不行动。
annotations.example: He made no move to take the paper.

annotations.explain: may not 表示可能不是，而非禁止；refer to 指谈及、对应或指涉。
annotations.example: These numbers may not refer to the same shipment.

annotations.explain: check with someone 表示向某人确认，而 check something 表示检查某物。
annotations.example: We need to check with the warehouse clerk.

annotations.explain: back then 指过去某一时期，常与 now 形成对比。
annotations.example: We need records from back then.

annotations.explain: must 在这里表示强推测而非义务；can't just ... and decide ... 用来否定仓促结论。
annotations.example: A name on a list doesn't mean he must be guilty.

annotations.explain: 句末 I see 可表达“我看出来了”，具体可能是赞许也可能是讥讽；需按人物关系判断。
annotations.example: You've been busy, I see.

annotations.explain: 固定表达 have time on one's hands，常有没事可做的意味。
annotations.example: With business slow, he had time on his hands.

annotations.phrase: chose not to pursue the matter
annotations.explain: choose not to + 动词表达刻意不做；pursue the matter 指继续追查或追责。
annotations.example: They chose not to pursue the complaint.

annotations.phrase: The moment those words left his mouth
annotations.explain: the moment ... left his mouth 是富有画面感的时间从句，强调立即反应。
annotations.example: The moment the words left my mouth, I regretted them.

annotations.explain: that's no way to + 动词，用于批评行为或说话方式。
annotations.example: That's no way to treat a guest.

annotations.explain: since when + be/do ...? 常作质疑立场或权利的反问，而非真的问时间。
annotations.example: Since when is honesty a favor?

annotations.explain: grant 指正式给予或批准，此处搭配 favor 暗示谢临舟把正常权利说成恩典。
annotations.example: Freedom is not a favor granted by one person.

annotations.explain: backtrack 指遇到阻力后收回或修改先前说法，比 say something else 更强调退让。
annotations.example: He backtracked when the evidence appeared.

annotations.explain: drag someone into something 表示让别人卷入麻烦，带非自愿色彩。
annotations.example: Don't drag your family into the dispute.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时被动 had been commissioned，强调在当前谈话之前已被委托。
annotations.example: The firm had been commissioned to transport grain.

annotations.explain: check ... for accuracy 是文件核验常用搭配，不等于内容必然真实。
annotations.example: Please check the figures for accuracy.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时被动表达此前形成的状态；leave blank 表示有意不填写。
annotations.example: The signature line had been left blank.

annotations.explain: proprietor 是较正式的经营者或所有者称呼，和店员或管事不同。
annotations.example: The proprietor must sign the form.

annotations.explain: vouch for someone/something 表示保证其可靠或真实，不只是“解释一下”。
annotations.example: I won't vouch for records I haven't checked.

annotations.explain: merely = only，但往往用于有意淡化某项行为的重要性；本处带推卸风险的言外之意。
annotations.example: He said the paper merely confirmed the date.

annotations.explain: attach something to something 是固定搭配；与任意日期账册关联会改变签字风险。
annotations.example: Someone could attach the statement to a later report.

annotations.explain: freeze 在动作描写中指突然停住，不是结冰；in midair 表示悬在空中。
annotations.example: Her hand froze in midair.

annotations.phrase: bring in whoever received the grain
annotations.explain: bring in 指请人参与或带人进来；whoever 引导名词性从句，充当宾语。
annotations.example: Bring in whoever signed the receipt.

annotations.phrase: How does getting my mother to sign this help anyone
annotations.meaning: 让我娘签字究竟能帮到谁
annotations.explain: getting my mother to sign this 整个动名词短语作主语；get + 人 + to do 是促使某人做事，和 have + 人 + 动词原形（安排某人做事）不同。
annotations.example: How does hiding the truth help anyone?

annotations.explain: find an opening 可以指找到时机或突破口；此处并非找到一扇门。
annotations.example: She waited until she found an opening to speak.

annotations.explain: the least someone can do 是常见施压/请求句型，表示最低限度的合理要求。
annotations.example: The least you can do is hear her out.

annotations.explain: nearly + 过去式表示事情几乎发生但实际未发生；常用于喜剧反应。
annotations.example: I nearly dropped the cup.

annotations.explain: want + 宾语 + 形容词/副词表示希望事情处于某种状态；over = 结束了。
annotations.example: She wanted the argument over.

annotations.explain: as + 副词 + as 引导程度比较；这里 badly 是“迫切”而不是“很差”。
annotations.example: He wanted answers as badly as I did.

annotations.explain: instead 用于说明原本可能采取的行为被另一种行为替代。
annotations.example: Instead, he asked about the missing letter.

annotations.explain: 单词独立成句时语气可能是直接、拒绝进一步解释，而非简单少字。
annotations.example: “Did he promise you anything?” “Nothing.”

annotations.explain: spite someone 指出于怨气故意让对方不快；与 jealousy 不同。
annotations.example: He thought I was doing it to spite him.

annotations.explain: reason with someone 指通过讲道理劝说对方，不能简单用 reason someone。
annotations.example: There's no reasoning with him when he's angry.

annotations.explain: get someone's attention 是固定搭配；在这里揭示谢临舟自我中心的误读。
annotations.example: She wasn't trying to get his attention.

annotations.explain: make + 人 + 形容词是使役结构，jealous 在感情语境指嫉妒或吃醋。
annotations.example: He thought she was trying to make him jealous.

annotations.explain: must be + 形容词可以表示强推测；这里是第一人称讽刺，不是真的同情。
annotations.example: It must be exhausting to suspect everyone.

annotations.explain: take something up with someone 表示向某人提出问题、投诉或当面交涉。
annotations.example: I'll take the mistake up with the manager.

annotations.explain: depending on ... 表示条件依赖；whom 作介词 on 的宾语，语体较正式。
annotations.example: The rules don't change depending on whom you trust.

annotations.explain: smile fades from one's face 是小说常见细微表情描写。
annotations.example: The smile faded from her face.

annotations.explain: befriend 意为主动与某人交朋友，比 be friends with 更侧重建立关系的动作。
annotations.example: He wondered whether he'd befriended the wrong person.

annotations.explain: 省略结构 she was 后省去了上下文已知的形容词 good，避免重复且强调立场。
annotations.example: “Is he innocent?” “I never said he was.”

annotations.phrase: find out what the accounts actually show
annotations.meaning: 查清账目真正说明了什么
annotations.explain: find out + 疑问词从句；what ... show 不是问“展示什么画面”，而是证据支持哪些事实。
annotations.example: We need to find out what the report actually says.

annotations.explain: Only + 状语置于句首引起主句部分倒装：Only after ... did ...；本句是典型例子。
annotations.example: Only after he left did I relax.

annotations.explain: begin to + 动词；feel weak 结合现场的压力表示紧张后的身体反应。
annotations.example: Once outside, I began to feel weak.

annotations.explain: 形容词单独作答，省略 I was；比 scared 强烈，形成角色坦率反差。
annotations.example: “Were you afraid?” “Terrified.”

annotations.explain: 条件句 If + 过去式 与 might + 动词原形构成假设的后果，侧重当时可能发生的情况。
annotations.example: If I stayed silent, he might blame us.

annotations.phrase: pin all eight thousand shi on me
annotations.meaning: 把八千石全赖到我头上
annotations.explain: pin something on someone 表示将责任、罪名推到某人身上。
annotations.example: They tried to pin the mistake on her.

annotations.explain: even if 表示即使在假设条件下结果仍不变，通常带夸张或强调。
annotations.example: Even if we hurried, we'd miss the meeting.

annotations.explain: get + 过去分词可构成非正式被动；在这里是人物夸张玩笑，不能视为现实建议。
annotations.example: If anyone gets blamed, it'll be me.

annotations.explain: be torn between A and B 指在两种反应/选择间摇摆；laughing 与 crying 平行。
annotations.example: He looked torn between relief and anger.

annotations.explain: dawdle 指磨蹭、拖时间；命令句 Stop + doing 表示停止某行为。
annotations.example: Stop dawdling or we'll be late.

annotations.explain: barely 表示几乎没有达到或才刚达到；We had barely ... when ... 是常见紧接发生句式。
annotations.example: We had barely sat down when the door opened.

annotations.explain: fold something into + 形状，描述结果；folded into ... 可作后置分词修饰语。
annotations.example: She handed me a letter folded into a square.

annotations.explain: slip something under ... 强调轻巧、隐蔽地放入，不一定是滑倒。
annotations.example: He slipped a note under the door.

annotations.explain: I thought + 从句 常表示过去的误判，现在知道并非如此。
annotations.example: I thought it was a menu, not a warning.

annotations.explain: There was ... 是存在句；用 only one sentence 制造悬疑焦点。
annotations.example: There was only one name on the page.

annotations.explain: be signed with + 名字/符号描述署名形式，也可说 signed by + 人名。
annotations.example: The note was signed with a single initial.

annotations.explain: tighten around 指围绕某物收紧，常用来写人物因紧张而不自觉握紧东西；不直接说 I was nervous，也能让读者感到情绪变化。
annotations.example: Her fingers tightened around the cup.

annotations.meaning: 那个没说出姓名的帮手难道……
annotations.explain: Could + 主语 + 动词引导的疑问在这里表达不确定的猜测，而不是“有能力吗”。
annotations.example: Could the messenger still be nearby?

annotations.explain: overlook 在地点描述里指俯瞰或朝向；不要和 overlook = 忽略混淆。
annotations.example: We chose a room overlooking the harbor.

annotations.explain: look past someone 可指目光越过某人寻找后方情况；不同于忽视某人的抽象义。
annotations.example: She looked past me toward the door.

annotations.explain: 对前问的省略式回答，原句可补全 I didn't take the originals；英语对话常省略已知部分。
annotations.example: “Did you bring the documents?” “Only copies.”

annotations.explain: check someone's finances 意为检查财务状况；此处是打趣温梨紧盯证据。
annotations.example: Stop checking my finances every time we meet.

annotations.explain: vanish 强调突然、不留痕迹地消失；at once = 立即。
annotations.example: Her smile vanished at once.

annotations.explain: along 表示沿某条线或方向；crease 是纸或布的折痕。
annotations.example: She folded the map along its creases.

annotations.explain: owe someone an explanation 是固定表达，表示有义务向某人交代。
annotations.example: You owe her an explanation.

annotations.phrase: slipped the note into her sleeve
annotations.explain: slip something into ... 常表达不引人注意地放入。
annotations.example: He slipped the key into his pocket.

annotations.explain: a great many + 复数可数名词，强调数量不少，略带书面色彩。
annotations.example: I still have a great many questions.

annotations.explain: what 引导名词性从句作主语，结构 what's most important is that ...。
annotations.example: What's most important is that nobody gets hurt.

annotations.explain: no third person 指除目前知情的两人之外不得再让第三方看到；third 是序数词，这里强调扩大知情范围会危及写信人。
annotations.example: Make sure no third person hears about this.

annotations.explain: go + 形容词表示状态变化，如 go quiet, go pale；went still 描写突然不动。
annotations.example: She went still when she saw the seal.

annotations.explain: follow someone's gaze 是高频小说叙事搭配，意为沿对方目光寻找所看物。
annotations.example: I followed his gaze to the window.

annotations.explain: plain clothes 形容非制服着装，在侦查语境中有特定意味，但不能据此推断身份。
annotations.example: Two guards waited in plain clothes.

annotations.explain: I'd = I had；过去完成时标示“看到动作”发生在当前茶馆场景之前。
annotations.example: I'd seen that handwriting before.

annotations.explain: 过去式被动 were followed 聚焦被跟踪者，隐藏未知施事者。
annotations.example: Were you followed on the way here?

annotations.phrase: I thought you were the one
annotations.explain: I thought ... 表示之前的判断，the one 后省略语境已知的被跟踪对象。
annotations.example: I thought you were the one who called.

annotations.explain: in one gulp 是喝东西时常用固定搭配，表示一饮而尽。
annotations.example: He finished the tea in one gulp.

annotations.explain: by 在 leave by + 出口/路线 中强调离开的途径；与 through the back door 的穿过动作相关，但前者侧重路线选择。
annotations.example: We left by the side entrance to avoid the crowd.

annotations.explain: alley 为小巷；back alley 更强调偏僻、少人走动，剧情中解释路线安全权衡。
annotations.example: The back alley was deserted.

annotations.phrase: go out onto the main street
annotations.explain: go out onto 强调从建筑/小巷进入开放街道，onto 有移动到表面的方向感。
annotations.example: We stepped out onto the main street.

annotations.phrase: And you think nothing can happen
annotations.explain: And you think ...? 常作为挑战对方推论的口语反问，而非中立询问。
annotations.example: And you think he'll tell us the truth?

annotations.explain: at least 用于承认方案不完美，但保留一个最低限度的好处；witnesses 指目击者。
annotations.example: It won't be safe, but at least there'll be witnesses.

annotations.phrase: Somehow, that didn't make me feel any safer
annotations.explain: Somehow 表示“说来也怪”，但此处略带讽刺；make + 人 + feel + 形容词是常见使役结构。
annotations.example: Somehow, his promise didn't make me feel better.

scenes.title: 茶肆会面
scenes.alt: 傍晚茶肆中，身着桃粉衣的姜明月与青绿衣的温梨隔桌相坐，低声谈论纸条。

scenes.title: 糖人摊疑踪
